title: powerkit design specification
description: One study design for a power analysis. Every front door (design forms, model builder, assistant) writes one of these; the engine reads only this. The schema checks structure. Checks that need arithmetic (e.g. that path values imply an R-squared below 1) are done by validate_spec() in R.
$comment: spec_version 0.1. When the format changes, add a new version rather than changing the meaning of an existing one: old saved specs must keep running.

design.description: Family of design. Together with 'template' it decides the backend.

template.description: The specific model within the design family. Allowed values depend on 'design'.

variables.description: The variables in the model, keyed by their role (X, Y, M, W, A, B, M1, ...). Labels are the user's own names and are used in the diagram and write-up.

population.description: The assumed population values. Its fields depend on 'design' and 'template'.

type.description: continuous = a score or scale; binary = two groups or yes/no; count = a number of events (0, 1, 2, ...); categorical = several unordered categories; between_factor / within_factor = an experimental factor varied between or within participants.

label.description: The user's own name for the variable.

levels.description: Names of the groups, categories or conditions, in order.

reliability.description: Reliability of the measure (e.g. Cronbach's alpha or omega), between 0 and 1. Omit for a perfectly reliable measure.

effect_justification.description: Why the effect size is what it is: it feeds the write-up and prevents unexamined 'medium effect' defaults. 'none' records honestly that no effect size can be justified (for example with a fixed sample size). The source, the user's reasoning, is optional in the spec; the app asks for it before a plan is saved or exported.

source.description: Where the number comes from, in the user's words (e.g. a reference, a decision rule).

adjustment.description: Any correction applied to the source effect (e.g. 'halved for publication bias'). Required for prior_study unless safeguard power is used.

safeguard.description: Safeguard power (Perugini, Gallucci & Costantini, 2014): plan with the lower bound of a two-sided confidence interval around one earlier study's effect size. For prior_study and pilot_study, with the one-sample, paired and independent t-tests and the correlation. The population value given is the earlier estimate; validation replaces it with the safeguard effect and records the estimate here.

n.description: The earlier study's number of participants (one-sample, paired, correlation).

n1.description: The earlier study's size of group 1 (independent groups).

n2.description: The earlier study's size of group 2 (independent groups).

protection.description: The chance that the true effect is at least the safeguard effect: 0.8 (the 60% interval) by default; 0.95 uses the 90% interval.

estimate.description: Filled in by powerkit: the earlier study's estimate, before the safeguard effect replaced it in the population.

conversion.description: The effect size as published in another form, converted with the effectsize package into the effect this design uses (Cohen's d for the one-sample and independent t-tests, d_z for the paired t-test, r for the correlation, partial eta-squared for a between-participants ANOVA given that way). Give the conversion instead of the population effect: validation fills that in and records it as 'result'.

from.description: The form of the published effect: a t statistic, an F statistic, r, Cohen's d, an odds ratio or Cohen's f. Which forms a design accepts: independent t-test t, F (one numerator df), r, odds_ratio; one-sample t-test t; paired t-test t, F (one numerator df); correlation t, F (one numerator df), d, odds_ratio; between-participants ANOVA given by partial eta-squared (oneway_between, 2x2_between, factorial_between with population > metric 'eta_squared') F with both dfs, f.

df.description: The numerator degrees of freedom of an F statistic converted into an ANOVA's partial eta-squared.

df_error.description: The error (denominator) degrees of freedom, for t and F.

n1.description: Optional: group 1's size, for r and d with two groups of unequal size (equal groups are assumed without it).

result.description: Filled in by powerkit: the converted effect, which is also the population value.

target_test.description: The one effect the power analysis is about, and how it is tested.

path.description: Mediation only: the indirect path being tested, e.g. 'X->M1->M2->Y'.

weights.description: Contrasts only: one weight per level of the factor, in the order of its levels. The weights must add up to 0, and at least one must not be 0. Their scale doesn't matter: (-3, -1, 1, 3) and (-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5) give the same power.

alpha.description: Significance level (two-sided unless 'alternative' says otherwise). Required for every test except the Bayes factor t-tests (method 'bayes_factor'), which have none.

alternative.description: Direction of the test. Only basic tests with a direction can be one-sided.

evidence_threshold.description: Bayes factor t-tests only (method 'bayes_factor'): the Bayes factor that counts as strong evidence, as BF10 (for an effect over no effect); power is the probability that BF10 reaches it. Default 10, bfpwr's default (powertbf01(k = 1/10), its BF01 threshold, which its help calls Jeffreys' threshold for strong evidence).

prior_scale.description: Bayes factor t-tests only: the scale of the Cauchy analysis prior on the standardised effect under the alternative (the Jeffreys-Zellner-Siow Bayes factor). Default 1/sqrt(2) (about 0.707), bfpwr's default (powertbf01(pscale = 1/sqrt(2))).

goal.description: sample_size: smallest n reaching 'power'. power: power at a fixed 'n'. sensitivity: smallest detectable effect at 'n' with 'power'. 'n' is the total number of participants analysed (after attrition). Generic tests (design 'generic_test') have no n: power is for the noncentrality given, and sensitivity is the noncentrality needed for 'power'.

power.description: Target power, as a proportion (0.90, not 90).

options.description: Run settings and cross-cutting options. All optional; the engine applies and records defaults.

attrition.description: Expected proportion of recruited participants who will not be analysed (0.10 for 10%). Used to turn the analysed n into a recruitment target.

nrep.description: Monte Carlo replications per sample size.

seed.description: Random seed, recorded with every result.

ci_draws.description: Monte Carlo draws (or bootstrap resamples) used to form each confidence interval for an indirect effect.

allocation_ratio.description: Two-group designs only (independent t-test, two proportions, two correlations, measurement invariance): size of the second group divided by the size of the first (1 = equal groups).

cell_ratio.description: 2 x 2 between-participants ANOVA only: the relative size of each cell, two rows (levels of A) of two positive whole numbers (levels of B); for example [[1, 1], [2, 2]] puts twice as many people at A's second level. goal > n is split in this ratio, so it must give whole cells. Unequal cells are simulated with Superpower::ANOVA_power() (ANOVA_exact() takes equal cells only), with Superpower's Type III sums of squares.

proportions_formula.description: Two proportions only, with method exact: z_test (the default) is the z test of two proportions with pooled variance under the null and no continuity correction, as in G*Power, via stats::power.prop.test() for equal groups and pwrss::power.z.twoprops() for unequal groups; arcsine is pwr's formula with Cohen's h (pwr.2p2n.test()).

method.description: How power is computed. exact: exact calculation for the specified population (the default for ANOVA designs, via Superpower; for basic tests other than Welch's t-test, via pwr's analytic formulas; for one proportion and McNemar's test, via pwrss's exact tests; for multiple regression, via pwrss's F test; and for Fisher's exact test, the goodness-of-fit test, two correlations and ANCOVA, via pwrss's formulas). For Welch's t-test, exact uses pwrss's analytic formula and must be requested. The rank tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis) have no exact method. simulation: Monte Carlo simulation with nrep replications (the default for every other design, and for Welch's t-test; available for the t-tests, correlation, two proportions, the chi-square test and ANOVA designs on request, and the only method for the rank tests).

variance.description: A variance, which must be above 0.

matrix_2x2_numbers.description: Two rows (levels of A) of two numbers (levels of B).

cell_sd.description: One standard deviation for all cells, or a 2x2 array of cell SDs (rows = levels of A).

paths.description: Standardised path coefficients keyed 'From->To' (e.g. 'X->M'). Product terms are named by joining the two variables: 'XW->M', 'MW->Y'. Every path in the template must be given; use 0 for no effect.

template_one_sample_t.description: One-sample t-test of a mean against 0 (in SD units).

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as d. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out d from them.

d.description: Cohen's d: (population mean - test value) / SD. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: the expected mean, the fixed value it is tested against, and the SD.

test_value.description: The fixed value the mean is tested against.

sd.description: The SD of the outcome, above 0.

score_shape.description: Rank tests only: the shape of the scores powerkit simulates, in SD units, with the effect a shift of that shape. For the signed-rank test it is the shape of the scores (one sample) or of the within-person differences (paired), which the test assumes are symmetric, so 'skewed' isn't offered. 'normal' (the default); 'heavy_tailed': a t distribution with 3 df, rescaled to SD 1, so extreme scores are more common than under a normal distribution.

effect_sd.description: Bayes factor t-tests only: how uncertain the expected effect is, as the SD of a normal design prior centred on the effect (d) in the same SD units. 0 (the default) plans for exactly that effect, as power analysis usually does.

template_independent_t.description: Two independent groups compared on a continuous outcome.

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as d. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out d from them.

d.description: Cohen's d: (mean of group 2 - mean of group 1) / pooled SD. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: each group's expected mean and the SD within a group (one SD for both groups).

mean_1.description: The expected mean of group 1 (X's first level).

mean_2.description: The expected mean of group 2 (X's second level).

sd.description: The SD of the outcome within a group, taken as the same in both groups, above 0.

score_shape.description: Rank tests only: the shape of the scores in every group, in SD units; groups differ only by a shift of that shape (their means). 'normal' (the default); 'skewed': a chi-square distribution with 10 df, standardised to mean 0 and SD 1 (as in Spower's p_wilcox.test() examples); 'heavy_tailed': a t distribution with 3 df, rescaled to SD 1, so extreme scores are more common than under a normal distribution.

effect_sd.description: Bayes factor t-tests only: how uncertain the expected effect is, as the SD of a normal design prior centred on the effect (d) in the same SD units. 0 (the default) plans for exactly that effect, as power analysis usually does.

template_paired_t.description: The same participants measured in two conditions.

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as dz. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out dz from them.

dz.description: Cohen's d_z: mean of the within-person differences (second condition minus first, in the order of X's levels) / SD of the differences. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: the expected mean in each condition, and either the SD of the differences (second minus first) or the SD of the outcome (the same in both conditions) with the correlation between the two measurements.

mean_1.description: The expected mean in the first condition (X's first level).

mean_2.description: The expected mean in the second condition (X's second level).

sd_difference.description: The SD of the within-person differences (second minus first), above 0.

sd.description: The SD of the outcome in each condition, taken as the same in both, above 0.

r.description: The correlation between the two measurements.

score_shape.description: Rank tests only: the shape of the scores powerkit simulates, in SD units, with the effect a shift of that shape. For the signed-rank test it is the shape of the scores (one sample) or of the within-person differences (paired), which the test assumes are symmetric, so 'skewed' isn't offered. 'normal' (the default); 'heavy_tailed': a t distribution with 3 df, rescaled to SD 1, so extreme scores are more common than under a normal distribution.

effect_sd.description: Bayes factor t-tests only: how uncertain the expected effect is, as the SD of a normal design prior centred on the effect (dz) in the same SD units. 0 (the default) plans for exactly that effect, as power analysis usually does.

template_correlation.description: Pearson correlation between two continuous variables, tested against 0.

method.description: 'pearson' (the default): Pearson's r, by formula (pwr). 'spearman' or 'kendall': Spearman's rho or Kendall's tau, simulated with Spower's p_r(method = ...) on bivariate normal scores whose Pearson correlation is population > r.

template_two_proportions.description: Two independent groups compared on a yes/no outcome.

p1.description: Proportion of 'yes' in the first group.

p2.description: Proportion of 'yes' in the second group.

method.description: z_test: the z test of two proportions (by formula, or simulated on request). fisher_exact: Fisher's exact test, by pwrss's exact power calculation (power.exact.fisher()).

template_chi_square_independence.description: Chi-square test of association between two categorical variables.

probabilities.description: Proportion of the population in each cell: one row per level of X, one column per level of Y. Must add up to 1.

template_2x2_between.description: Two between-participants factors, each with two levels. Cell sizes are equal unless options > cell_ratio gives their relative sizes.

metric.description: 'raw' or 'standardised': the effect is given by group means (in the outcome's units or in SD units) and the SD. 'eta_squared': it is given by the partial eta-squared of the effect tested ('eta_squared'), as in G*Power.

eta_squared.description: With metric 'eta_squared': the partial eta-squared of the effect tested (target_test > effect; for one factor, its eta-squared), treated as the population value, as G*Power and pwrss take it. powerkit then computes power with pwrss's F test (power.f.ancova()) instead of from group means. A published estimate tends to be larger than the true effect; omega-squared, if reported, is less biased.

template_2x2_mixed.description: Factor A varies between participants, factor B within participants; each has two levels.

r.description: Correlation between the two repeated measurements (levels of B) within a participant.

template_mixed.description: One factor A varies between participants, one factor B within participants (for example group by time), with at least one of them having three or more levels; a 2 x 2 design uses template 2x2_mixed. Groups are equal in size; the SD is the same in every cell and the correlation is the same between every pair of B's levels, so sphericity holds.

means.description: Expected cell means: one array per level of A (rows), each with one mean per level of B, in the order of the factors' levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation in every cell (the same in every cell).

r.description: Correlation between any two levels of B within a participant (the same for every pair).

template_factorial_between.description: Two crossed factors A and B, both between participants, with at least one of them having three or more levels (a 2 x 2 design uses template 2x2_between). Every cell is a different group of people, all equal in size, and the SD is the same in every cell.

metric.description: 'raw' or 'standardised': the effect is given by group means (in the outcome's units or in SD units) and the SD. 'eta_squared': it is given by the partial eta-squared of the effect tested ('eta_squared'), as in G*Power.

means.description: Expected cell means: one array per level of A (rows), each with one mean per level of B, in the order of the factors' levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation in every cell (the same in every cell).

eta_squared.description: With metric 'eta_squared': the partial eta-squared of the effect tested (target_test > effect; for one factor, its eta-squared), treated as the population value, as G*Power and pwrss take it. powerkit then computes power with pwrss's F test (power.f.ancova()) instead of from group means. A published estimate tends to be larger than the true effect; omega-squared, if reported, is less biased.

template_factorial_within.description: Two crossed factors A and B, both within participants: everyone is measured in every combination of their levels (a two-factor repeated-measures ANOVA, 2 x 2 or larger). The SD is the same in every cell and the correlation is the same between every pair of cells, so sphericity holds.

means.description: Expected cell means: one array per level of A (rows), each with one mean per level of B, in the order of the factors' levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation in every cell (the same in every cell).

r.description: Correlation between a participant's scores in any two cells (the same for every pair).

template_factorial_three.description: Three crossed factors A, B and C, each either between participants (different people at each level) or within participants (everyone at every level): a three-factor ANOVA, 2 x 2 x 2 or larger. The SD is the same in every cell; with any within factor, the correlation between a participant's scores in any two cells is the same for every pair, so sphericity holds. Every between-participants cell has the same number of people.

means.description: Expected cell means: one array per level of A, each holding one array per level of B, each with one mean per level of C, in the order of the factors' levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation in every cell (the same in every cell).

r.description: Only with at least one within-participants factor (and then required): the correlation between a participant's scores in any two cells (the same for every pair).

template_two_way.description: Y regressed on X, W and their product XW. Parametrised by correlations, as in InteractionPoweR.

r_XW_Y.description: Correlation between the product term XW and Y: the interaction effect.

template_three_way.description: Y regressed on X, W, Z, their three two-way products and the three-way product XWZ. Parametrised as in InteractionPoweR's power_interaction_3way_r2(): correlations among the true scores, and the standardised coefficient of XWZ.

r_XW_Y.description: Correlation between the product XW and Y.

r_XZ_Y.description: Correlation between the product XZ and Y.

r_WZ_Y.description: Correlation between the product WZ and Y.

b_XWZ.description: Standardised regression coefficient of the three-way product XWZ: the effect tested, in InteractionPoweR's parametrisation (b.x1x2x3).

template_process_4.description: PROCESS model 4: simple mediation (one mediator, named M) or parallel mediation (mediators M1, M2, ...).

^M[1-9]?$.description: mediators named M (one mediator) or M1, M2, ... (several)

x_prob.description: Yes/no X only: the proportion of people in X's second level (power4mome's rbinary_rs(p1 =)). 0.5 (equal groups) if omitted. The paths from X are per SD of X, as power4mome rescales X to SD 1.

residual_correlations.description: Parallel mediation only: correlations between the mediators' residuals, keyed 'M1<->M2'. Omitted pairs are 0.

template_process_6.description: PROCESS model 6: serial mediation through M1, M2 (up to M4), with every forward path.

^M[1-4]$.description: mediators named M1, M2, ... (up to M4), in causal order

x_prob.description: Yes/no X only: the proportion of people in X's second level (power4mome's rbinary_rs(p1 =)). 0.5 (equal groups) if omitted. The paths from X are per SD of X, as power4mome rescales X to SD 1.

^M[1-9]?$.description: mediators named M (one mediator) or M1, M2, ... (parallel mediators)

correlations.description: Correlation between X and W, keyed 'X<->W'. Omitted means 0 (e.g. X randomised).

residual_correlations.description: Parallel mediators only: correlations between the mediators' residuals, keyed 'M1<->M2'. Omitted pairs are 0.

path.description: With several mediators: whose index of moderated mediation is tested, as 'X->Mk->Y'.

template_one_proportion.description: One group's proportion of 'yes' compared with a fixed value, by the exact binomial test.

p.description: Expected proportion of 'yes' in the population.

p0.description: The fixed value the proportion is compared with (the null hypothesis).

template_mcnemar.description: The same people (or matched pairs) measured twice on a yes/no outcome, compared by McNemar's exact test.

p_first_only.description: Proportion of people who answer 'yes' in the first condition only (yes, then no): one of the two discordant proportions.

p_second_only.description: Proportion of people who answer 'yes' in the second condition only (no, then yes): the other discordant proportion.

template_oneway_between.description: One between-participants factor with three or more levels (one-way ANOVA, omnibus F test). Group sizes are equal.

metric.description: 'raw' or 'standardised': the effect is given by group means (in the outcome's units or in SD units) and the SD. 'eta_squared': it is given by the partial eta-squared of the effect tested ('eta_squared'), as in G*Power.

means.description: Expected mean of each group, in the order of the factor's levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation within each group (the same in every group).

sds.description: Welch's F only (target_test > method 'welch_f'): the SD of each group, in the order of the factor's levels, in the means' units. Give this or 'sd' (the same SD in every group).

score_shape.description: Rank tests only: the shape of the scores in every group, in SD units; groups differ only by a shift of that shape (their means). 'normal' (the default); 'skewed': a chi-square distribution with 10 df, standardised to mean 0 and SD 1 (as in Spower's p_wilcox.test() examples); 'heavy_tailed': a t distribution with 3 df, rescaled to SD 1, so extreme scores are more common than under a normal distribution.

eta_squared.description: With metric 'eta_squared': the partial eta-squared of the effect tested (target_test > effect; for one factor, its eta-squared), treated as the population value, as G*Power and pwrss take it. powerkit then computes power with pwrss's F test (power.f.ancova()) instead of from group means. A published estimate tends to be larger than the true effect; omega-squared, if reported, is less biased.

template_oneway_within.description: One within-participants factor with three or more levels: the same people in every condition (one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, omnibus F test, sphericity assumed). The SD is the same in every condition and the correlation is the same between every pair of conditions.

means.description: Expected mean in each condition, in the order of the factor's levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation in each condition (the same in every condition).

r.description: Correlation between any two conditions' measurements within a participant (the same for every pair).

template_oneway_contrast.description: A planned comparison (contrast) between the levels of one between-participants factor: a weighted combination of the group means, tested against 0. Trend tests (linear, quadratic) are contrasts with the matching weights. Group sizes are equal.

means.description: Expected mean of each group, in the order of the factor's levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation within each group (the same in every group).

template_r2_zero.description: Linear multiple regression (fixed predictors): is R-squared greater than 0? The F test of all predictors together.

r2.description: Expected R-squared of the model with all the predictors. 0 is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

predictors.description: Number of predictors in the model.

template_r2_increase.description: Linear multiple regression (fixed predictors): does adding a set of predictors increase R-squared? The F test of the added set.

r2_full.description: Expected R-squared of the full model (all the predictors).

r2_reduced.description: Expected R-squared of the model without the tested set (0 if the tested set is the only predictors).

predictors_total.description: Number of predictors in the full model.

predictors_tested.description: Number of predictors in the tested set (added to the reduced model).

template_generic_t.description: Generic t test: power from a noncentrality parameter and degrees of freedom (pwrss::power.t.test()).

variables.description: Generic tests have no variables; leave this empty ({}).

ncp.description: Noncentrality parameter under the alternative hypothesis.

template_generic_f.description: Generic F test: power from a noncentrality parameter and numerator and denominator degrees of freedom (pwrss::power.f.test()).

variables.description: Generic tests have no variables; leave this empty ({}).

ncp.description: Noncentrality parameter under the alternative hypothesis.

template_generic_chi_square.description: Generic chi-square test: power from a noncentrality parameter and degrees of freedom (pwrss::power.chisq.test()).

variables.description: Generic tests have no variables; leave this empty ({}).

ncp.description: Noncentrality parameter under the alternative hypothesis.

template_generic_z.description: Generic z test: power from the mean of the z statistic under the alternative (its noncentrality), with SD 1 (pwrss::power.z.test()).

variables.description: Generic tests have no variables; leave this empty ({}).

ncp.description: Noncentrality parameter under the alternative hypothesis.

template_chi_square_gof.description: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test: one categorical variable's proportions compared with fixed proportions (equal, unless given).

probabilities.description: Expected proportion of the population in each category of Y, in the order of its levels. Must add up to 1.

null_probabilities.description: The fixed proportions they are compared with (the null hypothesis), in the same order. Must add up to 1. Optional: equal proportions if left out, as pwrss's probs.to.w() assumes.

template_two_correlations.description: Two independent groups compared on the correlation between X and Y (Fisher's z test).

r1.description: Correlation of X with Y in the first group.

r2.description: Correlation of X with Y in the second group.

template_overlapping_correlations.description: One group: two correlations that share a variable, X with Y and X with Z, compared (Steiger's z test for dependent, overlapping correlations; G*Power's 'two dependent Pearson r's, common index').

r_X_Y.description: Correlation of X with Y: the first of the two correlations compared.

r_X_Z.description: Correlation of X with Z: the second of the two correlations compared.

r_Y_Z.description: Correlation of Y with Z. Not tested, but it sets how strongly the two compared correlations depend on each other.

template_nonoverlapping_correlations.description: One group: two correlations with no variable in common, X1 with Y1 and X2 with Y2, compared (Steiger's z test for dependent, non-overlapping correlations; G*Power's 'two dependent Pearson r's, no common index'), for example the same two measures at two time points.

r_X1_Y1.description: Correlation of X1 with Y1: the first of the two correlations compared.

r_X2_Y2.description: Correlation of X2 with Y2: the second of the two correlations compared.

r_X1_X2.description: Correlation of X1 with X2 (not tested).

r_X1_Y2.description: Correlation of X1 with Y2 (not tested).

r_Y1_X2.description: Correlation of Y1 with X2 (not tested).

r_Y1_Y2.description: Correlation of Y1 with Y2 (not tested).

template_one_variance.description: The variance of one group compared with a fixed value (the chi-square test of one variance). The effect is the ratio of the two.

var.description: Expected variance of Y in the population.

var0.description: The fixed variance it is compared with (the null value). Equal variances (no effect) are allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

template_two_variances.description: Two independent groups compared on the variance of Y (the F test of two variances). The effect is the ratio of the two.

var1.description: Variance of Y in the first group.

var2.description: Variance of Y in the second group. Equal variances (no effect) are allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

template_paired_variances.description: The same people measured twice, compared on the variance of Y (the Pitman-Morgan test: the correlation between the sum and the difference of the two measurements is zero exactly when their variances are equal). Simulated with Spower's p_r() on bivariate normal scores. goal > n is the number of people.

var1.description: Variance of Y in the first measurement.

var2.description: Variance of Y in the second measurement. Equal variances (no effect) are allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

r.description: The correlation between the two measurements.

template_oneway_ancova.description: One between-participants factor with two or more levels, adjusting for one or more covariates (one-way ANCOVA, omnibus F test; Shieh's method, covariates treated as random). Group sizes are equal.

means.description: Expected adjusted mean of each group (adjusted for the covariates), in the order of the factor's levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation of the outcome within each group, before adjusting for the covariates (the same in every group).

r2_covariates.description: Proportion of the outcome's variance the covariates explain (R-squared).

template_factorial_ancova.description: Two crossed between-participants factors A and B, adjusting for one or more covariates (two-way ANCOVA; Shieh's method, covariates treated as random): either main effect or the interaction. Every cell is a different group of people, all equal in size, and the SD is the same in every cell.

means.description: Expected adjusted cell means (adjusted for the covariates): one array per level of A (rows), each with one mean per level of B, in the order of the factors' levels.

sd.description: Standard deviation of the outcome within each cell, before adjusting for the covariates (the same in every cell).

r2_covariates.description: Proportion of the outcome's variance the covariates explain (R-squared).

template_single_predictor.description: Logistic regression of a yes/no outcome Y on one predictor X (a score or a yes/no group), optionally adjusted for other predictors: the Wald z test of X's coefficient.

odds_ratio.description: Odds ratio for X: per standard deviation of X for a score (X is taken as standardised), or the second level of X against the first for a yes/no group. 1 (no effect) is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

base_prob.description: Proportion with Y = yes (Y's second level) when X is at its mean (a score) or in X's first level (a yes/no group).

x_prob.description: Yes/no X only: the proportion of people in X's second level. 0.5 (equal groups) if omitted.

r2_other_predictors.description: R-squared of X on the other predictors in the model (0 if omitted, or if X is the only predictor). The other predictors' own effects aren't needed.

template_single_predictor_count.description: Poisson regression of a count outcome Y on one predictor X (a score or a yes/no group), optionally adjusted for other predictors: the Wald z test of X's coefficient.

rate_ratio.description: Rate ratio for X: the multiple of the event rate per standard deviation of X for a score (X is taken as standardised), or for the second level of X against the first for a yes/no group. 1 (no effect) is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n.

base_rate.description: Expected number of events per unit of exposure when X is at its mean (a score) or in X's first level (a yes/no group).

mean_exposure.description: Mean exposure per person: the time, distance or number of opportunities over which the events are counted. 1 if omitted, so the base rate is the expected count per person.

x_prob.description: Yes/no X only: the proportion of people in X's second level. 0.5 (equal groups) if omitted.

r2_other_predictors.description: R-squared of X on the other predictors in the model (0 if omitted, or if X is the only predictor). The other predictors' own effects aren't needed.

template_sem_model_fit.description: Structural equation model fit: the power of the chi-square test of exact fit to reject a model whose misfit in the population is a given RMSEA, by semPower::semPower.postHoc() (effect.measure 'RMSEA'). The model is described by its degrees of freedom ('df'), or, for a confirmatory factor analysis, by its number of items ('indicators') and of correlated factors ('factors'), each item loading on one factor; semPower::semPower.getDf() then counts the df. goal > n is the total number of participants analysed.

variables.description: A model-fit power analysis needs no variables; leave this empty ({}).

rmsea.description: The misfit the test should detect, as the population RMSEA (root mean square error of approximation) of the model. Above 0: semPower refuses an RMSEA of 0 (a model that fits exactly).

df.description: The model's degrees of freedom. Give this, or 'indicators' and 'factors', not both.

indicators.description: Confirmatory factor analysis: the number of items (observed variables).

factors.description: Confirmatory factor analysis: the number of factors, which are allowed to correlate. Each item loads on one factor.

template_sem_invariance.description: Measurement invariance of one factor across two groups (semPower::semPower.powerMI()) or, with population > over 'occasions', the same people on two occasions (semPower::semPower.powerLI()): the power of the chi-square difference (likelihood ratio) test to reject metric invariance (equal loadings; compared with the configural model) or scalar invariance (equal intercepts; compared with the metric model). The factor is measured by 'indicators' items, each with the standardised loading 'loading' in both groups, except that the last 'noninvariant' items have the loading 'loading_group2' in the second group (metric) or intercepts shifted by 'intercept_difference' item SDs in the second group (scalar). Factors are identified by fixing the first group's factor variance (and mean) only, as lavaan does. goal > n is the total number of participants analysed: across two groups, split by options > allocation_ratio (default 1); over two occasions, the people measured both times.

variables.description: Needs no variables; leave this empty ({}).

over.description: 'groups' (the default): two groups of different people. 'occasions': the same people measured twice, as in a longitudinal study.

stability.description: Occasions only: the correlation between the factor on the two occasions (how stable people's standing is). Required with over 'occasions'.

level.description: The level of invariance tested: 'metric' (equal loadings, against the configural model) or 'scalar' (equal intercepts, against the metric model).

indicators.description: The number of items measuring the factor.

loading.description: The standardised loading of every item in the first group (and of the invariant items in the second).

noninvariant.description: How many items differ between the groups (at least one item must not).

loading_group2.description: Metric invariance: the standardised loading of the differing items in the second group (or on the second occasion).

intercept_difference.description: Scalar invariance: how far the differing items' intercepts are shifted in the second group (or on the second occasion), in item SD units.

template_sem_factor_correlation.description: The correlation between two factors of a confirmatory factor analysis, against zero, by semPower::semPower.powerCFA(nullEffect = 'cor = 0'): the power of the chi-square difference (likelihood ratio) test of the model with the correlation fixed at 0 against the model with it free (1 df). Each factor is measured by its own items, all with the same standardised loading. goal > n is the total number of participants analysed.

variables.description: Needs no variables; leave this empty ({}).

r.description: The correlation between the two factors.

indicators.description: The number of items measuring each factor: two whole numbers.

loadings.description: The standardised loading of each factor's items: two numbers.

template_sem_latent_regression.description: A latent outcome regressed on one to five latent predictors, by semPower::semPower.powerRegression(): the power of the chi-square difference (likelihood ratio) test of one standardised slope against zero (1 df). Every factor is measured by 'indicators' items with the standardised loading 'loading'; the predictors all correlate 'predictor_correlation' (default 0). goal > n is the total number of participants analysed.

variables.description: Needs no variables; leave this empty ({}).

slopes.description: The standardised slope of each latent predictor.

predictor_correlation.description: The correlation between every pair of predictors (default 0).

tested.description: Which slope is tested, counting from 1 (default 1).

indicators.description: The number of items measuring each factor (the outcome and every predictor).

loading.description: The standardised loading of every item.

template_cluster_randomised.description: Cluster-randomised trial: whole groups (classes, clinics, teams) are assigned to one of two conditions, the same number of groups in each, and a score is compared between the conditions. The t test of the difference between conditions with the variance inflated by the design effect, by powertools::crt.parallel.cont(). goal > n is the total number of participants analysed: a whole number of groups of population > cluster_size, the same number of groups in each condition. With population > metric 'proportion', the outcome is yes/no and powertools' crt.parallel.bin() gives the z test of the log odds ratio from a mixed-effects logistic model.

metric.description: 'standardised': a score outcome, the effect given as Cohen's d. 'proportion': a yes/no outcome, the effect given as the proportion of 'yes' in each condition.

d.description: Cohen's d: (mean in the second condition - mean in the first) / the outcome's total SD (between and within groups together), as powertools defines it (delta / sd). 0 is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n, or for a sensitivity analysis.

icc.description: Intraclass correlation of the outcome: the proportion of its total variance that lies between groups, the same in both conditions. 0 means people in the same group are no more alike than people in different groups.

cluster_size.description: Number of participants analysed in each group (the average, if group sizes vary).

cluster_size_sd.description: Standard deviation of the group sizes, if they vary (0, the default, for groups of equal size). powertools adjusts power for the loss of efficiency.

p1.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the first condition (powertools' pc).

p2.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the second condition (powertools' pt).

sigma_u.description: Yes/no outcome: the SD, on the log-odds scale, of the groups' random intercepts (powertools' sigma.u): how much the groups' proportions differ.

baseline_r2_within.description: A baseline score (for example, a pre-test) adjusted for in the analysis: the proportion of the outcome's variance within groups (between people in the same group) that it explains, an R-squared from 0 to below 1 (powertools' RsqW). Leave out for no adjustment.

baseline_r2_between.description: With a baseline score: the proportion of the variance between the groups' averages that the baseline explains (powertools' RsqB, which its formula applies to the between-group variance: 1 + (m (1 - RsqB) - 1) ICC). Required with baseline_r2_within.

template_multisite.description: Multisite trial: within each group (school, clinic, team), people are randomised to one of two conditions, half to each, and a score is compared between the conditions. The t test of the average difference between conditions, with degrees of freedom from the number of groups, by powertools::multisite.cont(). goal > n is the total number of participants analysed: a whole number of groups of population > cluster_size. With population > metric 'proportion', the outcome is yes/no and powertools' multisite.bin() gives the z test of the log odds ratio from a mixed-effects logistic model.

metric.description: 'standardised': a score outcome, the effect given as Cohen's d. 'proportion': a yes/no outcome, the effect given as the proportion of 'yes' in each condition.

d.description: Cohen's d: (mean in the second condition - mean in the first) / the outcome's total SD (between and within groups together), as powertools defines it (delta / sd). 0 is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n, or for a sensitivity analysis.

icc.description: Intraclass correlation of the outcome: the proportion of its total variance that lies between the groups' averages (powertools' icc0). 0 means people in the same group are no more alike than people in different groups.

icc_effect.description: The proportion of the outcome's total variance that comes from the difference between conditions varying from group to group (powertools' icc1). 0 means the effect is the same in every group.

cluster_size.description: Number of participants analysed in each group, both conditions together, half in each (the average, if group sizes vary).

cluster_size_sd.description: Standard deviation of the group sizes, if they vary (0, the default, for groups of equal size). powertools adjusts power for the loss of efficiency.

p1.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the first condition (powertools' pc).

p2.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the second condition (powertools' pt).

sigma_u.description: Yes/no outcome: the SD, on the log-odds scale, of the effect (the log odds ratio) across groups (powertools' sigma.u).

baseline_r2_within.description: A baseline score (for example, a pre-test) adjusted for in the analysis: the proportion of the outcome's variance within groups (between people in the same group) that it explains, an R-squared from 0 to below 1 (powertools' RsqW; multisite.cont()'s Rsq). Leave out for no adjustment.

template_group_treatment.description: Individually randomised group treatment trial: people are randomised one by one to two conditions, and those in the second condition receive it in groups (for example, group therapy compared with individual treatment as usual), so only the second condition is clustered. The same number of people in each condition. A score is compared by powertools::irgtt.cont() (a t test with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, the variance of the grouped condition inflated by the design effect 1 + (m - 1) * ICC), or, with population > metric 'proportion', a yes/no outcome by powertools::irgtt.bin() (the z test of the difference in proportions, with the same design effect). goal > n is the total number of participants analysed: a whole number of groups of population > cluster_size in the second condition, and as many people again in the first.

metric.description: 'standardised': a score outcome, the effect given as Cohen's d. 'proportion': a yes/no outcome, the effect given as the proportion of 'yes' in each condition.

d.description: Cohen's d: (mean in the second, grouped condition - mean in the first) / the outcome's total SD, taken to be the same in both conditions (powertools' Theta = 1). 0 is allowed, to check the Type I error rate at a fixed n, or for a sensitivity analysis.

p1.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the first condition, delivered individually (powertools' p1).

p2.description: Yes/no outcome: the proportion of 'yes' in the second condition, delivered in groups (powertools' p2).

icc.description: Intraclass correlation in the grouped condition: the proportion of the outcome's variance there that lies between the groups. 0 means people in the same group are no more alike than people in different groups.

cluster_size.description: Number of participants analysed in each group of the second condition. The first condition has as many people in all as the second.

template_tost_independent.description: Equivalence (TOST) for two independent groups: is the difference in means between -bound and +bound?

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as d. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out d from them.

d.description: The expected true difference, as Cohen's d: (mean of group 2 - mean of group 1) / pooled SD. 0 if no difference is expected, which is the most favourable case. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: each group's expected mean and the SD within a group (one SD for both groups), and the equivalence bound in the same units.

mean_1.description: The expected mean of group 1 (X's first level).

mean_2.description: The expected mean of group 2 (X's second level).

sd.description: The SD of the outcome within a group, taken as the same in both groups, above 0.

bound.description: The equivalence bound in the outcome's own units: the effect is equivalent to none when the difference lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.
The equivalence bound, in the same standardised units as the expected effect: the effect is equivalent to none when it lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.

template_tost_paired.description: Equivalence (TOST) for the same participants in two conditions: is the mean within-person difference between -bound and +bound?

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as dz. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out dz from them.

dz.description: The expected true mean difference, as Cohen's d_z: mean of the within-person differences (second condition minus first) / SD of the differences. 0 if no difference is expected, which is the most favourable case. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: the expected mean in each condition, and either the SD of the differences (second minus first) or the SD of the outcome (the same in both conditions) with the correlation between the two measurements, and the equivalence bound in the same units.

mean_1.description: The expected mean in the first condition (X's first level).

mean_2.description: The expected mean in the second condition (X's second level).

sd_difference.description: The SD of the within-person differences (second minus first), above 0.

sd.description: The SD of the outcome in each condition, taken as the same in both, above 0.

r.description: The correlation between the two measurements.

bound.description: The equivalence bound in the outcome's own units: the effect is equivalent to none when the difference lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.
The equivalence bound, in the same standardised units as the expected effect: the effect is equivalent to none when it lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.

template_tost_one_sample.description: Equivalence (TOST) for one mean: is the difference between the mean and a fixed value between -bound and +bound?

metric.description: 'standardised': the effect is given as d. 'raw': it is given in the outcome's own units (population > raw), and powerkit works out d from them.

d.description: The expected true difference, as Cohen's d: (population mean - test value) / SD. 0 if no difference is expected, which is the most favourable case. With metric 'raw', powerkit works it out from population > raw.

raw.description: The effect in the outcome's own units: the expected mean, the fixed value it is tested against, and the SD, and the equivalence bound in the same units.

test_value.description: The fixed value the mean is tested against.

sd.description: The SD of the outcome, above 0.

bound.description: The equivalence bound in the outcome's own units: the effect is equivalent to none when the difference lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.
The equivalence bound, in the same standardised units as the expected effect: the effect is equivalent to none when it lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.

template_tost_correlation.description: Equivalence (TOST) for a correlation: is the correlation between -bound and +bound? Two one-sided z tests on Fisher's z scale, by TOSTER::power_z_cor(alternative = 'equivalence') (an approximation, as for the correlation test). goal > n is the number of people.

r.description: The expected true correlation (0 if none is expected, the most favourable case).

bound.description: The equivalence bound, as a correlation. The equivalence bound: the effect is equivalent to none when it lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.

template_tost_two_proportions.description: Equivalence (TOST) for two proportions: is the difference p2 - p1 between -bound and +bound? Two one-sided z tests, by TOSTER::power_twoprop(alternative = 'equivalence'). Equal groups (TOSTER takes one group size). goal > n is the total number of people, split equally.

p1.description: The expected proportion in group 1 (X's first level).

p2.description: The expected proportion in group 2 (X's second level).

bound.description: The equivalence bound, as a difference in proportions. The equivalence bound: the effect is equivalent to none when it lies between -bound and +bound. Above 0.

template_noninf_independent.description: Non-inferiority for two independent groups: is group 2 (the new condition) no worse than group 1 by more than the margin? A one-sided t-test of d against -margin (or +margin when lower is better), by pwrss::power.t.student(alternative = 'one.sided', margin). goal > n is the total number of people, split by options > allocation_ratio.

d.description: The expected true difference, as Cohen's d: (mean of group 2 - mean of group 1) / pooled SD. 0 if the two are expected to be the same.

margin.description: The non-inferiority margin: the largest difference in the wrong direction (worse for the new condition) that would still be acceptable, in the same units as the effect. Above 0.

better.description: Whether higher values of the outcome are better ('higher', the default) or lower ones are ('lower', for example symptoms or relapse).

template_noninf_paired.description: Non-inferiority for the same people measured twice: is the second condition no worse than the first by more than the margin? A one-sided paired t-test of d_z against the margin, by pwrss::power.t.student(design = 'paired'). goal > n is the number of people.

dz.description: The expected true difference, as d_z: mean of the differences (second minus first) / SD of the differences.

margin.description: The non-inferiority margin: the largest difference in the wrong direction (worse for the new condition) that would still be acceptable, in the same units as the effect. Above 0.

better.description: Whether higher values of the outcome are better ('higher', the default) or lower ones are ('lower', for example symptoms or relapse).

template_noninf_one_sample.description: Non-inferiority for one mean against a reference value: is it no worse than the reference by more than the margin? A one-sided one-sample t-test, by pwrss::power.t.student(design = 'one.sample'). goal > n is the number of people.

d.description: The expected true difference from the reference value, as Cohen's d: (mean - reference) / SD.

margin.description: The non-inferiority margin: the largest difference in the wrong direction (worse for the new condition) that would still be acceptable, in the same units as the effect. Above 0.

better.description: Whether higher values of the outcome are better ('higher', the default) or lower ones are ('lower', for example symptoms or relapse).

template_noninf_two_proportions.description: Non-inferiority for two proportions: is group 2's proportion no worse than group 1's by more than the margin? A one-sided z test of p2 - p1 against the margin, by pwrss::power.z.twoprops(alternative = 'one.sided', margin). goal > n is the total number of people, split by options > allocation_ratio.

p1.description: The expected proportion in group 1 (the comparison).

p2.description: The expected proportion in group 2 (the new condition).

margin.description: The non-inferiority margin: the largest difference in the wrong direction (worse for the new condition) that would still be acceptable, in the same units as the effect. Above 0.

better.description: Whether higher values of the outcome are better ('higher', the default) or lower ones are ('lower', for example symptoms or relapse).

template_crossed_two_condition.description: Participants respond to many items (stimuli) in two conditions, with the condition varying within participants: a linear mixed model y ~ condition + (1 + condition | participant) + (1 | item), with the condition coded -0.5 and 0.5 so its coefficient is the difference between conditions. With population > item_design 'within', every item appears in both conditions and a by-item condition slope may be given. Simulated with simr's powerSim() on a model built by makeLmer(), testing the condition with lmerTest's Satterthwaite t test (simr's method 'sa'). goal > n is the number of participants; every participant responds to every item (in one condition each when items are between conditions, in both when within).

difference.description: The mean in X's second condition minus the mean in its first, in the outcome's units (the fixed effect of the condition). 0 is allowed, to check the Type I error rate.

sd_participant.description: SD of the participants' random intercepts: how much participants' average responses differ.

sd_participant_slope.description: SD of the participants' random condition slopes: how much the difference between conditions varies across participants.

r_participant.description: Correlation between participants' intercepts and condition slopes. 0 if omitted.

sd_item.description: SD of the items' random intercepts: how much items' average responses differ.

sd_item_slope.description: Items in both conditions only (item_design 'within'): SD of the items' random condition slopes. 0 if omitted.

sd_residual.description: SD of the residual: trial-to-trial variation within a participant and item.

items.description: Total number of items. With items between conditions, half are in each condition, so the number must be even.

item_design.description: 'between' (the default): each item appears in one condition only. 'within': every participant responds to every item in both conditions.

template_ordinal_two_groups.description: Two groups compared on an outcome in ordered categories, under proportional odds (Whitehead's method, via powertools::propodds()).

Y.description: The outcome: categorical, with its categories listed in order, lowest first.

probabilities.description: The share of group 1 in each category of Y, in the order of Y's levels; they must sum to 1.

odds_ratio.description: Odds of a higher category in group 2 relative to group 1, the same at every cut-point (proportional odds). 1 is no effect.

template_logistic_factorial.description: A yes/no outcome Y in a two-factor design with different people in every cell: logistic regression with both factors and their interaction (effect coding), the Wald chi-square test of one effect's coefficients on the log-odds scale, simulated with Spower's p_glm().

probabilities.description: Proportion with Y = yes (Y's second level) in each cell: one row per level of A, one value per level of B, in the order of their levels.
